title: Derivation of organoids from primary tumour tissue
author: Hazel Rogers
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bfvnjn5e

steps.title: Transfer tissue to glass dish
steps.instruction: Pour or pipette the tissue and its transport media into a glass petri dish; if infection status is unknown, open the transport container inside a microbiological safety cabinet. Use glass dishes to avoid tissue sticking to plastic grooves.

steps.title: Wash tissue with PBS
steps.instruction: Aspirate as much transport media as possible, add 10 mL PBS, aspirate, and repeat the PBS wash at least two more times (three washes for pancreas/oesophagus, five for colon). After the final wash aspirate residual PBS. If tissue fragments break apart and aspiration risks loss, transfer the tissue and PBS back to a 15 mL tube, centrifuge at 800 × g, °C, for 2 min, aspirate supernatant, resuspend in fresh PBS, and repeat the required number of washes.

substeps.instruction: Repeat wash (total 3 or 5 times depending on tissue).
After last wash, aspirate all PBS.
If tissue breaks up, transfer to 15 mL tube, centrifuge 800 × g, °C, 2 min, aspirate supernatant, resuspend in PBS, repeat washes.

steps.title: Add digestion buffer and mince tissue
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL digestion buffer to the tissue, then mince the tissue with a scalpel into pieces approximately 1–2 mm in diameter. Transfer the minced tissue and buffer into a 15 mL tube.

substeps.instruction: Cut tissue into 1–2 mm pieces with scalpel.

steps.title: Incubate tissue in digestion buffer
steps.instruction: Place the tube on a rotator and incubate at 37 °C for 60–120 minutes.

steps.title: Assess digestion under microscope
steps.instruction: Examine the incubation mixture under a microscope; the preparation should appear cloudy and consist of single cells or small clumps, indicating sufficient digestion.

steps.title: Filter digested tissue through strainer
steps.instruction: Transfer the digested mixture to a 50 mL tube through a 100 µm cell strainer, using a pestle to push remaining tissue through. Wash the original 15 mL tube with 10 mL PBS and add this wash to the 50 mL tube; repeat the wash once.

substeps.instruction: Pass digested sample through 100 µm strainer into 50 mL tube.
Use pestle to push remaining tissue through strainer.
Wash 15 mL tube with 10 mL PBS and add to 50 mL tube.

steps.title: First centrifugation of filtrate
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 50 mL tube at 800 × g, °C, for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet and repeat spin
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 30 mL PBS, and centrifuge again at 800 × g, °C, for 2 minutes.

steps.title: Final PBS wash and spin
steps.instruction: Aspirate supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 2.5 mL PBS, transfer to a 5 mL (or 15 mL) tube, wash the 50 mL tube with an additional 2.5 mL PBS and add to the small tube, then centrifuge at 800 × g, °C, for 2 minutes.

substeps.instruction: Wash 50 mL tube with 2.5 mL PBS and add to small tube.

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in 80% BME2
steps.instruction: Aspirate remaining supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 80 % BME2; use approximately 200 µL per well of a 6‑well plate (adjust volume based on pellet size). Dispense BME2 quickly to prevent premature solidification; keep on a cool block if needed, and verify cell density by pipetting one or two 15–20 µL droplets and inspecting under a microscope, adding more BME2 if the suspension is too dense.

substeps.instruction: Resuspend pellet in 80 % BME2 (≈200 µL per well).
Dispense quickly; keep on cool block if possible.
Pipette 1–2 droplets (15–20 µL) and check density.

steps.title: Plate BME2 suspension in 6‑well plate
steps.instruction: Using a P200 pipette, dispense the BME2‑cell suspension as 15–20 µL droplets into each well of a 6‑well plate, aiming for a total of ~200 µL per well.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 15–20 µL droplets into each well.
Ensure total volume per well ≈200 µL.

steps.title: Allow BME2 to solidify
steps.instruction: Place the plate in a 37 °C incubator with 5 % CO₂ for 15–30 minutes to allow the BME2 matrix to set.

steps.title: Prepare complete organoid media
steps.instruction: Prepare complete organoid culture media by adding, per millilitre of base media, 2 µL primocin, 10 µL penicillin‑streptomycin, and 1 µL Y‑27632 (rock inhibitor).

substeps.instruction: Add 2 µL primocin per mL media.
Add 10 µL penicillin‑streptomycin per mL media.
Add 1 µL Y‑27632 per mL media.

steps.title: Add media to plated organoids
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL of the prepared media to each well of the 6‑well plate.

steps.title: Incubate and maintain cultures
steps.instruction: Return the plate to the incubator; change media twice weekly until the organoids are ready for passage, keeping antibiotics and Y‑27632 in the media until the first passage.

substeps.instruction: Maintain antibiotics and Y‑27632 until first passage.
